paper: APPSC Group-I Preliminary (Screening Test) 2023, Notification 28/2022, Paper I – General Studies (GS/1G/100), held 08-01-2023

questions.s: During the Indus Valley Civilization, the beads manufacturing industry was located at
questions.x: Chanhudaro in Sindh was a specialised craft centre of the Harappans, with workshops for bead-making, shell-working and seal-making.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Select the correct statements about religious beliefs of the Rig Vedic Period :
I. Dyus was a celestial God of the Rig Vedic Aryans similar to Jupiter of the Greeks.
II. Prithvi was considered as the mother of all Gods.
III. Agni was worshipped as the intermediary of taking the offerings to the deities.
IV. Cow sacrifice was also the part of worship.
questions.x: Dyaus (sky father, the Greek Zeus/Jupiter), Agni as the messenger carrying offerings to the gods and animal (including cow) sacrifice are attested in the Rig Veda; Prithvi was the earth goddess, not the mother of all gods.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following schools of philosophies with their theories :
a. Sankhya   I. Predetermined fate theory
b. Vaisheshika   II. World was formed by the blending of nature
c. Lokayata   III. Considered Atom as basis of the world
d. Ajivika   IV. Advocated materialistic ideology
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Sankhya explains the world as evolving from Prakriti (nature) with Purusha, Vaisheshika's atomism treats atoms as the basis of the world, Lokayata (Charvaka) is materialist, and the Ajivikas believed in niyati, predetermined fate.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela gave the details of irrigation facilities provided in the Kalinga Region by
questions.x: The Hathigumpha inscription records that Kharavela extended a canal originally dug by a Nanda king (Mahapadma Nanda) three hundred years earlier.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Select the correct statements regarding the inscriptions of Ashoka :
I. They are in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic scripts.
II. The Monarch’s name was mentioned as Ashoka only in Maski and Gurjara inscriptions.
III. The XIII Rock edict mentioned the names of the five Greek Rulers as his contemporaries.
IV. The IV and V edicts mentioned the war of succession with his brothers.
questions.x: Ashoka's edicts are in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic; his personal name Ashoka appears only in the Maski and Gujarra edicts; Rock Edict XIII names five Greek kings. The edicts say nothing about a war of succession, so IV is wrong.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following books with their authors :
a. Prajnaparamita   I. Acharya Kundakunda
b. Samayasara   II. Sarvavarma
c. Lilavati Parinayam   III.Acharya Nagarjuna
d. Katantra Vyakaranam   IV. Kuthuhala
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Prajnaparamita literature is linked with Acharya Nagarjuna, Samayasara was written by Kundakunda, Lilavati Parinayam by Kuthuhala and the Katantra grammar by Sarvavarma.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following was not the feature of the Guilds during the Gupta Period ?
questions.x: Gupta-era guilds (shrenis) were autonomous bodies with their own rules, seals, militia and banking functions, so 'non-autonomous bodies' was not their feature.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
The account of Greek (Yavana) invasion during the reign of Pushyamitra Sunga is available in :
I. Gargi – Samhita
II. Patanjali – Mahabhashya
III. Kalidasa – Malavikagnimitra
IV. Visakhadatta – Mudrarakshasa
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Yavana invasion in Pushyamitra Sunga's time is mentioned in the Yuga Purana of the Gargi Samhita, Patanjali's Mahabhashya and Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitra; Mudrarakshasa deals with Chandragupta Maurya.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Choose the correct statement regarding Nalanda University at the time of Harshavardana :
o: Harshavardana donated 10,000 villages to the university.
The number of teachers in the university were 15,000.
Silabhadra was the Chancellor of the university.
The medium of instruction was Pali.
questions.x: Hiuen Tsang, who studied at Nalanda in Harsha's time, records Silabhadra as the head (chancellor) of the university; the other figures are wrong (about 100-200 villages, about 1,500 teachers, Sanskrit medium).
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following taxes :
Name Tax
a. Navidadere   I. Tax on Marriage
b. Melivamsam   II. Tax on Barbers
c. Manevana   III. Tax on Ploughs
d. Tudimeya   IV. Tax on Houses
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: As per the official key: Navidadere was the tax on barbers, Melivamsam on ploughs, Manevana on houses and Tudimeya on marriage (II, III, IV, I).
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Arrange the following temples of Ellora in chronological order according to their time of construction :
I. Ravan ki Khai
II. Kailasanatha
III. Dashavatara
IV. Dumar Lena
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: As per the official key, the Ellora sequence is Dashavatara (Cave 15), then Ravan ki Khai, then Dumar Lena, then the Kailasanatha temple built under the Rashtrakuta Krishna I.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following terms with their meaning related to village administration of the Cholas :
a. Variyam   I. Ward
b. Kudumba   II. Lottery system
c. Kudavolai   III. Member of the village assembly
d. Perumakkal   IV. Committee system
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The official key matches variyam with committee system, kudumbu with ward, kudavolai with member of the village assembly and perumakkal with lottery system (IV, I, III, II). Standard texts usually link kudavolai with the pot-ticket lottery, so this key is debatable.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following highways existed during the rule of Kakatiyas ?
I. Orugallu – Tripuranthakam – Nellore
II. Dwarasamudra – Ballari – Orugallu
III. Motupalli – Tripuranthakam – Ballari
IV. Palnadu – Nalgonda – Nekarikallu – Orugallu
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: As per the official key, the Motupalli-Tripuranthakam-Ballari and Palnadu-Nalgonda-Nekarikallu-Orugallu trade routes existed in Kakatiya times.
questions.subject: AP History & Culture

questions.s:
Which of the principles are common for Bhakti and Sufi movement ?
I. Monotheism
II. Asceticism
III. Religious tolerance
IV. Accepted the idol worship to some extent
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Bhakti saints and Sufis both stressed devotion to one God (monotheism), renunciation or simple ascetic living, and tolerance, while generally rejecting idol worship.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Choose the incorrect pair regarding the foreign chronicles of the Vijayanagara Period :
o: Abdur Razzaq – Described the conditions during the reign of Devaraya II
Domingo Paes – Described the rule of Krishna Devaraya
Caesar Frederick – Wrote about the conditions of Vijayanagara after the battle of Rakshasa Tangadi
Nikitin – Visited during the reign of Achyuta Devaraya
questions.x: The Russian traveller Nikitin visited the Bahmani kingdom in the 1470s, long before Achyuta Devaraya, so that pair is incorrect.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The Vijayanagra ruler who permitted Jesuits to build churches at Nellore and Chandragiri was
questions.x: Venkatapati Raya II of the Aravidu dynasty allowed Jesuit missionaries to build churches at Chandragiri and Nellore.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following incidents took place during the reign of Jahangir ?
I. The fifth Sikh Guru, Arjan Dev was sentenced to death
II. Victroy over Rajputs of Mewar
III. Annexation of Kabul and Kandahar
IV. Arrival of English East India Company to India
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Under Jahangir, Guru Arjan Dev was executed (1606), Mewar submitted (1615) and the English East India Company arrived (Hawkins 1608, Roe 1615); Kabul and Kandahar were not annexed in his reign (Kandahar was lost in 1622).
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following revenue officials during the reign of Akbar with their duties :
a. Amalguzar   I. Kept records of the revenue payable by the villages
b. Karkuns   II. Revenue Collector in-charge of a District
c. Qanungo   III. Accountant
d. Bitikchi   IV. Prepared the seasonal crop statistics
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: As per the official key (II, IV, I, III): the amalguzar was the district revenue collector, the karkuns prepared the seasonal crop statistics, the qanungo kept the records of revenue payable by villages and the bitikchi was the accountant.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The longest Trunk Road constructed by Shershah which still exists is
questions.x: Sher Shah's Sarak-i-Azam (later the Grand Trunk Road) ran from the Indus to Sonargaon in Bengal and still exists.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following books with their authors :
a. India at the Death of Akbar   I. Irfan Habib
b. The Agrarian System of Mughal India, 1556 – 1707   II. François Bernier
c. Travels in the Mogul Empire : AD 1656 – 1668   III. William Foster
d. Early Travels in India, 1583 – 1619   IV. Moreland
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: W.H. Moreland wrote India at the Death of Akbar, Irfan Habib The Agrarian System of Mughal India, Bernier the Travels in the Mogul Empire, and William Foster edited Early Travels in India.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The following historian contended that Taj Mahal is a combination of European and Asiatic genius :
questions.x: Vincent A. Smith argued that the Taj Mahal was the result of a combination of European and Asiatic genius.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following with the year they were formulated :
a. Famine Code   I. 1881
b. Vernacular Press Act   II. 1878
c. Charles Wood’s Despatch on Education   III. 1883
d. 1st Factory Act   IV. 1854
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Famine Code dates from 1883, the Vernacular Press Act from 1878, Wood's Despatch from 1854 and the first Factory Act from 1881.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Arrange the following incidents of Rebellion against East India Company in the State of Hyderabad in chronological order :
I. Attack of Turrebaz Khan on British Residence in Hyderabad
II. Imprisonment of Mubariz-ud-Daula in Golkonda Fort
III. In Aurangabad, 1st Contingent Cavalry was suspected, disarmed and arrested
IV. The rebellion of Raja Venkatappa Nayaka of Shorapur
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: As per the official key, the order is the imprisonment of Mubariz-ud-Daula, the Aurangabad cavalry mutiny of 1857, the attack on the Residency by Turrebaz Khan (July 1857) and then the revolt of Raja Venkatappa Nayaka of Shorapur.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following Presidents of Indian National Congress with their meetings :
a. Dadabhai Naoroji   I. Madras – 1887
b. Badruddin Tyabji   II. Bombay – 1889
c. George Yule   III. Allahabad – 1888
d. William Wedderburn   IV. Calcutta – 1886
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Dadabhai Naoroji presided at Calcutta (1886), Badruddin Tyabji at Madras (1887), George Yule at Allahabad (1888) and William Wedderburn at Bombay (1889).
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The following book was translated by Gandhiji with the title Sarvodaya :
o: Leo Tolstoy – The Kingdom of God is Within You
questions.x: Gandhiji translated John Ruskin's Unto This Last into Gujarati as Sarvodaya.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following newspapers with the persons associated with them :
a. Indian Sociologist   I. Virendra Chattopadhyay
b. Islamic Fraternity   II. Shyamji Krishna Varma
c. The Talwar   III. Muhammad Barkatullah
d. Swadesh Sevak   IV. G.D. Kumar
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Indian Sociologist was run by Shyamji Krishna Varma, Islamic Fraternity by Muhammad Barkatullah, Talwar by Virendranath Chattopadhyay and Swadesh Sevak by G.D. Kumar.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The idea of Indian Constituent Assembly was put forward for the first time by
questions.x: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Match the following authors with their works :
a. Al-Biruni   I. Tariqh-i-Firoz Shahi
b. Minhaj-us-Siraj   II. Tahqiq-i-Hind
c. Ziauddin Barani   III. The Rihla
d. Ibn Battuta   IV. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Al-Biruni wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind, Minhaj-us-Siraj Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Ziauddin Barani Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Ibn Battuta the Rihla.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following institutions were not established during the Non-Cooperation Movement ?
I. Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle
II. Jamia Millia Islamia, Delhi
III. Kashi Vidyapith, Benaras
IV. Aligarh Muslim University, Aligarh
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Jamia Millia Islamia and Kashi Vidyapith were founded during Non-Cooperation (1920-21), but the Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle (1915) and Aligarh Muslim University (1920 Act, from the 1875 MAO College) were not products of the movement.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: The Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the House of Commons by the British Prime Minister Attlee on
questions.x: The Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the House of Commons on 4 July 1947 and received royal assent on 18 July 1947.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the State Finance Commission ?
I. It is required to appoint a State Finance Commission once in five years.
II. It recommends the determination of taxes, duties, tolls and fees assigned to the Panchayats and Municipalities.
III. Article 243 deals with constitution of finance commission to review financial position of Panchayats.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Under Articles 243-I and 243-Y a State Finance Commission is set up every five years to review Panchayat and Municipal finances and recommend the sharing and assignment of taxes, duties, tolls and fees.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following Amendment(s) provide(s) for reservation in jobs and admissions ?
questions.x: The 77th Amendment (reservation in promotions), 81st (carry-forward backlog) and 82nd (relaxed qualifying marks) all concern reservation in jobs, so all are correct.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) :
The President is the executive power of the Union.
Reason (R) :
The executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.x: Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President, to be exercised directly or through subordinate officers, which explains the assertion.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statements related to the Central Administrative Tribunal are correct ?
I. It is a statutory body.
II. Its members are drawn from administrative background only.
III. It is not bound by the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure.
IV. Its jurisdiction covers the members of All-India services as well as Central services and Central Government posts.
V. It was set up in 1985.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The CAT is a statutory body set up in 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act; it is not bound by the Civil Procedure Code and covers All-India and Central services; its members include judicial members too.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following statements is not one of the powers of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly ?
o: He has no veto except in case of a tie.

A Speaker may be removed from office by a resolution of the Assembly passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly after fourteen days notice of the intention to move such a resolution.
The Speaker vacates his office if he ceases to be a member of the Assembly.
The Speaker will preside when a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration of the Assembly.
questions.x: The Speaker cannot preside while a resolution for his own removal is under consideration (Article 181), though he may speak and vote in the first instance.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
The powers of the Election Commission include which of the following ?
I. The Election Commission takes decisions on every aspect of conduct and control of elections from the announcement of elections to the declaration of results.
II. During the election period, the Election Commission can order the Government to dismiss some government officials.
III. When on election duty, Government officers work under the control of the Election Commission.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Election Commission controls the whole election process and officials on election duty work under it, but it cannot order the government to dismiss officials.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
What is/are the provision(s) to safeguard the autonomy of the Supreme Court of India ?
I. While appointing the Supreme Court Judges, the President of India has to consult the Chief Justice of India.
II. The Supreme Court Judges can be removed by the Chief Justice of India only.
III. The salaries of the Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India on which the legislature does not have to vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.x: Consultation with the CJI in appointments and charging judges' salaries on the Consolidated Fund protect judicial autonomy; judges are removed only by Parliament through impeachment, not by the CJI.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following are not included in the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court ?
I. A dispute between two or more States.
II. A dispute regarding elections to either House of the Parliament or that of Legislature of a State.
III. A dispute between the Government of India and a Union Territory.
IV. A dispute between the Government of India and one or more States.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Election disputes go to High Courts and Centre-Union Territory disputes are not federal disputes, so they are outside the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes, while investigating any matter or inquiring into any complaint, has the powers on the following matters :
I. It can receive evidences on affidavits.
II. It can requisition any public record from any court or office.
III. It can issue summons for the examination of witnesses and documents.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Under Article 338(8) the NCSC has the powers of a civil court: it can summon witnesses, requisition public records and receive evidence on affidavits.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) :
The Parliament of India consists of the President and two Houses.
Reason (R) :
The President is a part of the legislature even though he does not sit in Parliament except for the purpose of delivering his opening address.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.x: Article 79 says Parliament consists of the President and two Houses; the President is an integral part of the legislature though he does not sit in it, which explains the assertion.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following are among the Fundamental Duties of citizens laid down in the Indian Constitution ?
I. To protect the weaker sections from social injustice.
II. To develop scientific temper and spirit of inquiry.
III. To preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
IV. To safeguard public property and adjure violence.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.x: Article 51A includes developing scientific temper, preserving composite culture and safeguarding public property and abjuring violence; protecting the weaker sections is a Directive Principle (Article 46).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following entries of the Indian Constitution deals with the institutions for scientific or technical education financed by the Government of India, wholly or in part, and declared by Parliament, by law to be institutions of national importance ?
questions.x: Entry 64 of the Union List covers institutions for scientific or technical education financed by the Government of India and declared institutions of national importance by law.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Who said “India is not a nation in the traditional western sense but a comprehensive culture of continental scope compounded of a very large number of linguistic and religious entities, highly complex and often strongly antagonistic local cultures” ?
questions.x: As per the official key, the quotation is attributed to Carl Friedrich.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
The Constitution confers which of the following Articles that denies the rights to aliens (Foreign Citizens) ?
I. Articles 29 and 30
II. Article 19
III. Articles 23 and 24
IV. Article 16
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Articles 16, 19, 29 and 30 are available only to citizens, while Articles 23 and 24 protect all persons, including foreigners.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. The Preamble was enacted before the enactment of the entire Constitution.
II. The Preamble is a part of the Constitution but has no legal effect independently of other parts.
III. It is enforceble through Courts of Law.
IV. The Objectives Resolution by Jawaharlal Nehru finally became the foundation for the Preamble.
Which of the statements given above are incorrect ?
questions.x: As per the official key, I and III are incorrect: the Preamble was adopted last, after the rest of the Constitution, and it is not enforceable in courts of law.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
I. The PM CARES for Children Scheme was launched by the Prime Minister of India on 29th May, 2021 for the children.
II. It aims to support children who have lost both the parents or legal guardians or adoptive parents or surviving parent to Covid-19 pandemic.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The PM CARES for Children Scheme was announced on 29 May 2021 for children who lost both parents, legal guardians, adoptive parents or a surviving parent to Covid-19.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: With child labour being made illegal and right to education becoming a fundamental right for children, this right against exploitation has become more meaningful. Which of the following pairs of Articles provide for right to education and prohibition of child labour respectively ?
questions.x: Article 21A gives the right to education to children aged 6-14, and Article 24 prohibits employment of children below 14 in factories, mines and hazardous work.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements regarding GST :
I. GST will bring more transparency to direct tax laws.
II. GST was the 122nd Constitutional Amendment Bill introduced in the Parliament.
III. GST is a destination-based tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.x: GST is an indirect, destination-based tax introduced through the 122nd Constitution Amendment Bill (101st Amendment Act); it has nothing to do with direct tax laws.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which of the bodies recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes to be shared between the Centre and the States, and allocation between the States, the respective shares of such proceeds ?
questions.x: Under Article 280 the Finance Commission recommends the vertical and horizontal distribution of the net proceeds of shareable taxes between the Centre and the States.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following is not the function of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes ?
o: Providing constitutional protection to Scheduled Castes.
To submit the report to the Prime Minister related to the protection of Scheduled Castes.
To investigate any case that violates the interests of Scheduled Castes.
questions.x: The NCSC reports to the President, not the Prime Minister (Article 338(5)(d)); the other items are its functions.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following is not a function of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) ?
o: Conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union
questions.x: The UPSC is consulted on recruitment methods and disciplinary matters and conducts examinations, but it is not consulted on reservation of posts (Article 320(4)).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following subjects are listed in the 11th Schedule ?
I. Women and Child Development
II. Public Distribution System
III. Libraries
IV. Slum Improvement and Upgradation
V. Markets and Fairs
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: As per the official key, women and child development, public distribution system, libraries and markets and fairs are in the Eleventh Schedule; slum improvement belongs to the Twelfth.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the National Green Tribunal ?
I. It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
II. NGT is bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
III. NGT has six places of sitting throughout the country.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The NGT was set up under the NGT Act, 2010; it is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure and follows natural justice, and it sits at five places.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
With reference to the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, consider the following statements about National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) :
I. Judge of the Supreme Court can now be appointed as Chairperson of the Commission.
II. Term of the Chairperson and members shall be three years.
III. Chairperson and members shall be eligible for re-appointment.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: The 2019 amendment allowed any Supreme Court judge (not only a former CJI) to be Chairperson, reduced the term to three years and made members eligible for re-appointment.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements :
I. It was set up under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
II. Ministry of Welfare has notified five religious communities under “Minority” status, to date.
III. It can make recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards for the protection of minorities by Central or State Governments.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.x: The NCM was set up under the NCM Act, 1992 and recommends safeguards for minorities; six communities (including Jains since 2014) are notified, and by the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Recently, the term ‘Chicago Convention’ is frequently seen in the news. Which of the following sector is it associated with ?
questions.x: The Chicago Convention of 1944 established the International Civil Aviation Organization and the rules of international air navigation.
questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.s:
With reference to the Competition Commission of India, consider the following statements :
I. It is a statutory body established under Competition Act, 2002 as amended by the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2007.
II. It consists of a chairperson and five members appointed by the Central Government.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: The CCI is a statutory body under the Competition Act, 2002 as amended in 2007; it has a chairperson and six members, not five.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established on the recommendation of which of the following Committee ?
questions.x: NABARD was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: ‘World Competitiveness Index’ is released by which of the following organizations ?
questions.x: The World Competitiveness Yearbook/Ranking is published by the Institute for Management Development (IMD), Lausanne.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Kautilya categorizes the Governments and Heads of Departments into 18 tirthas. Amongst these “Dandapala” is the
questions.x: Among Kautilya's 18 tirthas, the Dandapala was the officer in charge of the army.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select your answer from the codes given below.
Assertion (A) :
There is a structural change in the composition of National Income in India.
Reason (R) :
The process of economic growth was initiated in India.
Codes :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A).
questions.x: As per the official key, economic growth leads to structural change in the composition of national income (shift from agriculture to industry and services), so R explains A.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: The economist who said that the “Net Social Product and the Social Income are one and the same thing” is
questions.x: J.R. Hicks held that the net social product and the social income are one and the same thing.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select your answer from the codes given below.
Assertion (A) :
